newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWIMMING-ISAKSSON TAKES MEN'S 100 BREASTSTROKE WORLD TITLE.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-ISAKSSON TAKES MEN'S 100 BREASTSTROKE WORLD TITLE.

text.p: Patrik Isaksson, roared on by his home fans, brought hosts Sweden their second gold medal of the world short-course swimming championships with a rousing victory in the men's 100 metres breaststroke on Friday.
Isaksson, the joint slowest qualifier, was unfazed by a false start which forced a restart to the race and charged straight into the lead in the outside lane one.
The Swede held his advantage at the halfway mark and hung on bravely to earn the host nation their second gold after Lars Frolander's victory in the men's 100 butterfly on Thursday.
Isaksson, who won the 50 breaststroke gold at the European short-course championships in Rostock last December, won in 59.99.
Stanislav Lupokhov of Russia took the silver in 1:00.05 and Germany's Jens Kruppa, who beat Isaksson to the 100 breaststroke gold in Rostock, claimed the bronze in 1:00.18.
